profile.headline: Collins Aerospace
profile.summary:
Entrepreneurial technologist with strong experience as an executive in early stage start-ups. Broad understanding of the business fundamentals of creating a start-up. Talent for understanding the big picture, including how products / companies provide value to customers and where those products fit within the market ecosystem. Superior strategic aptitude for creating the company vision and road map, mapping customer needs to product requirements, and clearly understanding the role of disruptive technologies as a means of penetrating a market, and creating a valuable set of components (products, software base, talent pool, intellectual property) that can be used to fuel further growth and expansion of the business.

Specialties: - Leadership of early-stage start-ups 
- Development of intellectual property
- Market analysis, Competitive analysis, Strategic planning 
- Technology Start-up Veteran, Engineering VP and CTO 
- System architecture, from embedded systems to servers
- Server and desktop virtualization
- Networking and storage networking technologies, including standards, protocols, hardware and software  
- software development, test, QA, and release

positions.title: CTO, Co-Founder
positions.description:
The company mission was to create a hardware / software solution that would dramatically alter the economics of scaling the delivery of stored content to users.
Participated in the company's funding and the process of interviewing and selecting the executive team.
Developed the initial architecture of the appliance.
Worked with Marketing to research and develop competitive analysis and ROI tools.
Assisted the board in re-structuring the company into a software and services company in 2004.

positions.title: CTO, Co-Founder
positions.description:
Designed the first products shipped, ARCNet adapters and Hubs. 
Designed most of the Token Ring hardware manufactured by TCC.
Implemented many of the device drivers for TCC network adapters, on several operating systems.
While at TCC, I assumed many roles, ranging  from individual contributor in hardware and software development, VP of Engineering and CTO. 
Gained direct, hands-on experience in almost every aspect of running a start-up.
Thomas-Conrad was acquired by Compaq Computer Corporation in 1995.
